extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for examiners (and practitioners) on nonstatutory double patenting, restriction/election of species, and related examination procedures (AIA and pre‑AIA), including when to use particular form paragraphs and how to determine patentable distinctness between claims, species, combinations, and subcombinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT publication pre‑Nov 29, 2000 not prior art under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the reference is a publication of an international application (PCT), including voluntary U.S. publication under 35 U.S.C. 122 of the national stage or a WIPO PCT publication, that has an international filing date prior to November 29, 2000, did not designate the United States or was not published in English by WIPO, do not use this form paragraph. Such a reference is not a prior art reference under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e). The reference may be applied under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a) or (b) as of its publication date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See form paragraphs 7.08.fti and 7.09.fti for treatment; be careful to determine the correct pre‑AIA/pre‑AIPA 102(e) date when the reference is an international application or national stage filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bracket insertion requirements in form paragraphs
rubrics_metrics.description: In specified form paragraphs, examiner must insert appropriate bracketed items (e.g., in bracket 3, insert --assignee--, --applicant--, or --joint inventor--; in bracket 1 insert claim numbers; in bracket 2 insert application number; in bracket 4 insert explanation of obviousness).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specific bracket instructions for each form paragraph (numeration varies by paragraph); see corresponding Examiner Notes for examples and where to draw explanations (e.g., MPEP §2144 for obviousness explanations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph precedence requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain form paragraphs must be preceded by other specified form paragraphs (e.g., this form paragraph must be preceded by either of form paragraphs 7.12.fti or 7.12.01.fti; some paragraphs must be preceded by form paragraph 7.03.aia; 7.21.aia must be preceded by 7.03.aia).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use a form paragraph unless its required preceding paragraph(s) have been used; check Examiner Notes for the exact required predecessor paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications with filing dates on/after March 16, 2013 special prerequisite
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications with an actual filing date on or after March 16, 2013, that claim priority to, or the benefit of, an application filed before March 16, 2013, certain form paragraphs must be preceded by form paragraph 7.06.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure AIA vs pre‑AIA treatment is correct; apply 7.06 where indicated to address cross‑dated priority situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identical subject matter and 35 U.S.C. 101 constraint
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 35 U.S.C. 101, two patents are not permitted to issue on identical subject matter. Any claims in the instant application directed to the same invention claimed in the reference should be rejected (or provisionally rejected if the reference has not yet issued as a patent) using form paragraphs 8.30 - 8.32.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also require applicant to resolve any issue of priority under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(g) and possibly pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(f) using form paragraph 8.27.fti. See MPEP § 804, subsection II.A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonstatutory double patenting rejection when not patentably distinct
rubrics_metrics.description: Any claims in the instant application that are directed to subject matter that is not patentably distinct from an invention claimed in the reference should be rejected (or provisionally rejected if the reference has not yet issued as a patent) on the grounds of nonstatutory double patenting using form paragraph 8.33 and at least one of form paragraphs 8.34 - 8.39.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the claimed invention is not patentably distinct, make appropriate nonstatutory double patenting rejections and consider requirements for terminal disclaimers or other remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional rejection (AIA) for copending application with common assignee/applicant/inventor (¶7.21.01.aia)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] is/are provisionally rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being obvious over copending Application No. [2] which has a common [3] with the instant application. The copending application would constitute prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) if published or patented; this rejection is based on a presumption of future publication or patenting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provisional rejection might be overcome by: (1) showing under 37 CFR 1.130(a) that subject matter disclosed in the copending application was obtained from the inventor/joint inventor; (2) showing under 37 CFR 1.130(b) of a prior public disclosure under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(B); or (3) a statement pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C) establishing common ownership/joint research agreement. See MPEP §717.02. Use only for applications filed on/after March 16, 2013 and preceded by 7.03.aia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional rejection (pre‑AIA) for copending application with common assignee/applicant/inventor (¶7.21.01.fti)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] is/are provisionally rejected under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a) as being obvious over copending Application No. [2] which has a common [3] with the instant application. The copending application would constitute prior art under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) if published or patented; the rejection is based on a presumption of future publication or patenting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provisional rejection might be overcome by: (1) showing under 37 CFR 1.132 that any invention disclosed but not claimed in the copending application was derived from the inventor/joint inventors (i.e., inventive entity); (2) showing a date of invention for the instant application prior to the pre‑AIA 102(e) date of the copending application under 37 CFR 1.131(a); or (3) showing copending application is disqualified under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(c). Use when copending application qualifies as prior art under pre‑AIA 102(e) and has common assignee/applicant/inventor; follow pre‑AIPA rules for international applications per Examiner Notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection (AIA) where applied reference only qualifies under 102(a)(2) with common ownership/inventor (¶7.21.02.aia)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] is/are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being obvious over [2]. The applied reference has a common [3] with the instant application and, based upon the earlier effectively filed date of the reference, it constitutes prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rejection may be overcome by the same means set forth for provisional rejections (37 CFR 1.130(a),(b); 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C) statement). Use only for applications filed on/after March 16, 2013, preceded by 7.03.aia, and only when the reference qualifies solely under 102(a)(2) (use 7.21.aia if 102(a)(1) applies). Do not use when the 102(b)(2)(C) exception applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection under 35 U.S.C. 103 'further in view of' (¶7.22.aia)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] is/are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over [2] as applied to claim [3] above, and further in view of [4].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be used only in applications filed on/after March 16, 2013 (preceded by 7.03.aia) and must be preceded by form paragraph 7.21.aia. An explanation of the rejection must follow this form paragraph (see MPEP §2144).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection (pre‑AIA) where applied reference only qualifies under pre‑AIA 102(e) (¶7.21.02.fti)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] is/are rejected under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a) as being obvious over [2]. The applied reference has a common [3] with the instant application and, based upon the pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) date of the reference, it constitutes prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rejection might be overcome by: (1) showing under 37 CFR 1.132 that any invention disclosed but not claimed in the reference was derived from the inventor (not an invention 'by another'); (2) showing a date of invention corresponding to subject matter disclosed in the reference prior to the reference's 102(e) date under 37 CFR 1.131(a); or (3) an oath/declaration under 37 CFR 1.131(c) of same ownership and prior inventor status. Do not use if the reference qualifies under pre‑AIA 102(a) or (b); apply pre‑AIPA rules where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission to Technology Center Director for double patenting rejections relying on parent application
rubrics_metrics.description: Every Office action containing a rejection on the ground of nonstatutory double patenting which relies on the parent application to reject the claims in a divisional application where the divisional application was filed because of a restriction requirement must be submitted to the Technology Center Director for approval prior to mailing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the rejection is disapproved by the Director, it shall not be mailed but other appropriate action shall be taken. See MPEP §1003 for further handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: §121 protection when restriction requirement in parent application
rubrics_metrics.description: When a claimed invention that was the subject of a restriction requirement is presented in a divisional application, a nonstatutory double patenting rejection cannot be applied to that claimed invention unless the restriction requirement was withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 121 shields those withdrawn claims in a later divisional application against rejection over a patent that issues from the original application; if the restriction requirement does not clearly set forth the line of demarcation, consonance may be lacking and §121 protection may not apply. See Geneva Pharmaceuticals, Applied Materials, Symbol Technologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consonance requirement for §121 protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 121 shields claims against a double patenting challenge if consonance exists between the divided groups of claims and an earlier restriction requirement. If a restriction requirement does not clearly set forth the line of demarcation, then challenged claims could not satisfy the consonance requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must assess whether the line of demarcation of the original restriction was maintained; loss of consonance can permit double patenting, but double patenting does not automatically follow if claims are patentably distinct or §121 requirements are otherwise met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact of Patent Term Extension (PTE) under 35 U.S.C. 156 on double patenting
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonstatutory double patenting does not invalidate any patent term extension (PTE) granted under 35 U.S.C. 156, if the claims are otherwise valid under its pre‑PTE expiration date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per Novartis AG v. Ezra Ventures LLC, a PTE pursuant to §156 is valid so long as the extended patent is otherwise valid without the extension; courts will not let a judge‑made doctrine cut off a statutorily authorized time extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of improper joinder under 35 U.S.C. 121
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 121 provides 'the validity of a patent shall not be questioned for failure of the Director to require the application to be restricted to one invention.' In other words, no patent can be held invalid for improper joinder of inventions claimed therein.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improper joinder at the Office does not itself invalidate a patent under §121; consider statutory protections when evaluating challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: General principles for determination of distinctness/independence (§806)
rubrics_metrics.description: (A) Where inventions are independent (no disclosed relation), restriction to one is ordinarily proper. (B) Where inventions are related as disclosed but are distinct as claimed, restriction may be proper. (C) Where inventions are related as disclosed but are not distinct as claimed, restriction is never proper. (D) A reasonable number of species may be claimed when there is an allowable claim generic thereto.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These summarize the core tests for restriction practice; see MPEP §§806.04–806.06 and §802.01 for criteria for patentably distinct inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare claimed subject matter to determine distinctness (§806.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: In passing upon questions of double patenting and restriction, it is the claimed subject matter that is considered and such claimed subject matter must be compared in order to determine the question of distinctness or independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A provisional election of a single species may be required where only generic claims are presented and the generic claims encompass a multiplicity of species making an unduly extensive and burdensome search necessary. See MPEP §803.02 and §808.01(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Single embodiment / same essential features — no restriction (§806.03)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the claims of an application define the same essential characteristics of a single disclosed embodiment of an invention, restriction therebetween should never be required because the claims are different definitions of the same disclosed subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If such claims are voluntarily presented in different applications having common inventor/assignee (no Office restriction), see MPEP §804–§804.02 for treatment; do not require restriction among claims that are merely alternative breadth definitions of the same embodiment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genus and species restriction rules (§806.04)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an application includes claims directed to different embodiments or species that could fall within the scope of a generic claim, restriction between the species may be proper if the species are independent or distinct. 37 CFR 1.141 provides that an allowable generic claim may link a reasonable number of species embraced thereby.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply election of species practice (37 CFR 1.146) in first action on applications with a generic claim and multiple patentably distinct species; if more than a reasonable number of species present, examiner may require restriction to not more than a reasonable number before taking further action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and effect of a generic claim (§806.04(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: A generic claim should read on each species; in general, a generic claim should require no material element additional to those required by the species claims, and each species claim must require all the limitations of the generic claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once a generic claim is allowable, species claims that require all limitations of the generic claim will ordinarily be allowable over the prior art; when species claims do not require all limitations, see MPEP §821.04(a) for further practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims limited to species — terminology and relationship to generic claims (§806.04(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims are definitions or descriptions of inventions; claims themselves are never species. A claim may be limited to a single disclosed embodiment (specific species claim) or encompass two or more embodiments (generic/genus claim). Species refer to different embodiments and may be independent or related.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether species are independent or related when deciding restriction or double patenting issues; see §806.04 and §806.04(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction between mutually exclusive species (§806.04(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: A requirement for restriction to a single species may be proper if the species are mutually exclusive: claims to different species are mutually exclusive if one claim recites limitations disclosed for a first species but not a second, and vice versa — i.e., the claims must not overlap in scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish non‑overlapping scope (no claim reads on the other) before requiring restriction between species.

rubrics_metrics.name: Species must be patentably distinct from each other (§806.04(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: In making a requirement for restriction in an application claiming plural species, the examiner should group together species considered clearly unpatentable over each other. If generic claims are allowable, applicant may claim additional species as provided by 37 CFR 1.141. If species are voluntarily presented in a different application (no election by Office), closely investigate for double patenting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If divisional claims arise consonant with an election to a species, 35 U.S.C. 121 may prohibit double patenting rejections; otherwise applicant may overcome rejections by terminal disclaimer (In re Goodman, In re Braithwaite).

rubrics_metrics.name: Generic claim filed after issuance of species claims — double patenting risk (§806.04(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a generic claim is presented in a separate application after the issuance of a patent claiming one or more species within the scope of the generic claim, the Office may reject the generic claim on the grounds of nonstatutory double patenting when the patent and application have at least one common inventor and/or are commonly assigned/owned (or subject to joint research agreement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may overcome such a rejection by filing a terminal disclaimer. See MPEP §804 and cited case law (In re Goodman, In re Braithwaite).

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal question for related inventions — distinctness decides restriction/double patenting (§806.05)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where two or more related inventions are claimed, the principal question is whether the inventions as claimed are distinct. If distinct, restriction may be proper. If not distinct, restriction is never proper. If nondistinct inventions are claimed in separate applications or patents, double patenting must be held, except where additional applications were filed consonant with a requirement to restrict.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider statutory class differences and whether one‑way or two‑way distinctness tests apply (see examples in §806.05(c) and §806.05(j)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Combination vs subcombination distinctness criteria (two‑way test) (§806.05(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: To support a requirement for restriction between combination and subcombination inventions, both two‑way distinctness and reasons for insisting on restriction are necessary — i.e., there would be a serious search burden (separate classification/status/field of search) and/or a serious examination burden (non‑prior art issues relevant to one invention but not the other).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventions are distinct if (A) the combination as claimed does not require the particulars of the subcombination for patentability (novelty/unobviousness), and (B) the subcombination can be shown to have utility either by itself or in another materially different combination. Provide evidence (classification, utility, claim scope) to support distinctness. See examples I (subcombination essential — no restriction) and II (subcombination not essential — restriction proper if other reasons exist).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of form paragraph 8.15 for combination‑subcombination restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: ¶ 8.15 Combination‑Subcombination — Inventions [1] and [2] are related as combination and subcombination. Inventions in this relationship are distinct if it can be shown that (1) the combination as claimed does not require the particulars of the subcombination as claimed for patentability, and (2) that the subcombination has utility by itself or in other combinations (MPEP §806.05(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 3 specify the limitations of the claimed subcombination not required by the claimed combination or evidence supporting the conclusion; in bracket 4 suggest separate utility. Conclude restriction requirement with form paragraph 8.21. If applicant elects a subcombination that is later found allowable, examine dependent claims per 37 CFR 1.104 and be alert to provisional double patenting rejections over the instant application.
